review_candidates.title: Substation Commissioning Engineer - CE141 / SR141 / TP141
review_candidates.description: Company Description Egis is a leading global architecture, consulting, construction engineering and operating firm. We work side by side with clients to build a more balanced, sustainable and resilient world. Omnia Projects, part of the Egis Group, are a UK-based engineering consultancy specialising in electricity Transmission and Distribution (T&D) providing engineering, project management and technical assurance. Project Description The successful individual will support and work with the inhouse project delivery team to provide works across several asset classes to include substations, underground cables, overhead lines and civils. This will cover at all system voltages from low voltage (LV) up to and including 132kV. Job Description Role Overview The Commissioning Engineer supports project-based works, portfolios of projects, and ad-hoc repairs, ensuring the commissioning and integration of protection, control, and SCADA systems across all distribution asset classes (overhead lines, underground cables, substations, civil works, and work programmes). The role involves undertaking all aspects of commissioning activities to ensure assets are fit for purpose and meet regulatory and customer obligations. Key Responsibilities Perform pre-commissioning inspection prior to off-load commissioning tests. Check detailed schematics against connections, protection, and tripping logic diagrams. Attend Factory Acceptance Testing and project-specific meetings as required. Conduct off-load commissioning checks, including: Witness testing of primary substation plant (circuit breakers, switches/disconnectors, transformers, voltage and current transformers). Insulation resistance, primary and secondary injection tests. Circuit logic tests against DC schematic diagrams. Testing integral relay logic. Protection relay checks (distance relays, feeder differential, transformer differential, frequency, G99 type, high impedance busbar, blocked busbar protection). Auto-reclose scheme checks. Intertripping and signalling equipment checks. Testing integration of protection systems with control and SCADA using DNP3 and IEC61850 protocols. Testing and proving relay programmable logic files, relay setting files, and DNP3 communication files. Interface with customers, internal and external resources. Complete all work in line with company objectives (time, cost, quality). Accurately record all time spent on projects and provide timely reports on progress and status. Provide guidance and support to other members of the Protection Commissioning Team. Use and update company data and information systems, including comprehensive commissioning records and on-site fault/defect investigations. Undertake duties under the CDM Regulations as Designer and/or Contractor. Qualifications Knowledge & Qualifications Minimum Higher National Certificate (HNC) in Electrical Engineering. TP141 OR SR141 OR CE141 Certification Essential Proven working history in the electricity distribution/transmission industry delivering protection commissioning, typically with 10+ years’ experience practicing as a Commissioning Engineer. Skills, experience, and detailed knowledge of protection on all distribution asset classes of switchgear, transformers, and feeders at all voltages up to and including 400Kv. High level of professionalism, able to work under pressure and to tight timescales. Strong preference for recent experience in commissioning protection systems associated with generation connections, including integration with legacy protection and control systems. Must either possess or be capable to successfully obtain and maintain the following Company Operational Authorisation requirements: A1 Access and Supervision to substations controlled by a level 3 key. A2.1 and A2.4 Access and Supervision to open compounds. O11.11 Testing & Commissioning of all Primary S/S & Bulk Supply Point protection up to & including 132kV. O11.18 Work on protection, control, and equipment including assisting an engineer with the testing & operation of relays and isolated plant. Willingness to travel between work locations, sites, and company/supplier offices. Current and valid UK driving licence. Additional Information Additional Information Services are delivered nationally. Expenses for travel and accommodation incurred for company needs will be paid separately, subject to company allowances and contract terms. The allocation and mix of project work may vary and will be determined by company priorities. All work should be performed in strict accordance with company processes, procedures, and industry best practice. If you decide to apply for an opportunity at EGIS, your application will be assessed based purely on your experience, the essential and desirable criteria, and your suitability for the role. We value each and everyone’s contribution as this builds our culture and means, if you work for EGIS, you will be included, listened to, and respected.

review_candidates.title: Site Acceptance Manager
review_candidates.description: Job Title Site Acceptance Manager Department Facilities Operations – Deployment Reports To Senior Director of Deployment, Facilities Operations Location: [Site location – to be confirmed] Position Type Full-Time, Permanent Travel Primarily site-based during build and handover; occasional travel (c.10–20%) to other Nscale sites, vendor/OEM factories for FAT and Nscale offices across Europe About Nscale Nscale is the GPU cloud engineered for AI. We provide cost-effective, high-performance infrastructure for AI start-ups and large enterprise customers. Nscale enables AI-focused companies to achieve superior results by reducing the complexity of AI development. Our GPU cloud bolsters technical capabilities and directly supports strategic business outcomes, including cost management, rapid innovation, and environmental responsibility. At Nscale, our Facilities Operations team plays a critical role in driving the safe, reliable and efficient operation of the data centre infrastructure that powers our GPU cloud – from first energisation of a new site through to steady-state live operations at scale. We thrive on a culture of relentless innovation, ownership, and accountability, where every team member takes pride in their work and drives it with excellence and urgency. As an Nscaler, you’ll build trust through openness and transparency, where everyone is inspired to do their best work. If you join our team, you’ll be contributing to building the technology that powers the future. About The Role We’re looking for a Site Acceptance Manager with exceptional planning, technical and stakeholder leadership skills to own the transition of our self-build data centre projects from construction into live operations. Reporting to the Senior Director of Deployment, you’ll plan, oversee and manage site acceptance end-to-end – from commissioning readiness and witness testing through to the formal handover of a complete, safe and fully documented facility to our operational teams. You’re comfortable leading at the interface between construction, commissioning and operations, making sound decisions under programme pressure and with incomplete information. You’re comfortable influencing without authority – holding contractors, commissioning agents, vendors and internal teams to an agreed acceptance standard. You have strong technical grounding in critical facility systems (power, cooling, controls and life safety) and can quickly get to the root of a defect or failed test. You’re a meticulous planner who is extremely organised and diligent, with a disciplined approach to documentation, punch lists and evidence of acceptance. You’re safety-first, and won’t accept a system into operations until it’s proven safe, complete and maintainable. You’re a self-starter, curious and quick to learn, comfortable bringing structure to a fast-scaling, high-growth environment. What You’ll Be Doing You’ll own the end-to-end site acceptance and construction-to-operations transition plan for Nscale’s self-build data centre projects, from pre-commissioning readiness through to final handover and early-life support. You’ll build and maintain an integrated acceptance and handover programme aligned to construction, commissioning (Levels 1–5 / IST) and customer go-live milestones, tracking progress and escalating risks to the Senior Director of Deployment. You’ll define acceptance criteria, handover requirements and readiness gates (e.g. Ready for Energisation, Ready for Commissioning, Ready for Service), agreeing them with design, construction, commissioning and operations stakeholders at project outset. You’ll oversee and witness commissioning activities – including factory acceptance tests (FAT), site acceptance tests (SAT) and integrated systems testing (IST) – ensuring results are evidenced, defects are captured and retests are completed. You’ll manage the punch list and defects process, prioritising and driving close-out of outstanding items with contractors and vendors before and after handover. You’ll ensure complete and accurate handover documentation – O&M manuals, as-built drawings, test certificates, asset registers, warranties, spares and statutory compliance certificates – is delivered, reviewed and accepted. You’ll lead operational readiness with Facilities Operations leadership, ensuring staffing, training, SOPs/MOPs/EOPs, CMMS asset and planned maintenance set-up, critical spares and service contracts are in place before go-live. You’ll coordinate vendor and OEM training and knowledge transfer so the operations team is confident and competent on every critical system they inherit. You’ll manage the formal transfer of site control – permit-to-work, LOTO and site safety responsibility – from the principal contractor to Nscale operations, ensuring a safe and controlled transition. You’ll chair acceptance and handover meetings, maintain RAID logs and provide clear, data-driven reporting on readiness status to senior leadership. You’ll oversee the defects liability and early-life support period, tracking warranty claims and capturing lessons learned to feed back into design standards and future builds. You’ll continuously improve Nscale’s acceptance and handover framework, templates and standards so they scale across a growing portfolio of sites.
